_comment: The SFO lens instance of the pilot pack (packs/pilot/lenses/sfo-cooperation.json; phase 6b prep, 2026-10-22): a lens from a text, the Serious Fraud Office's corporate guidance on self-reporting and co-operation, held at sources/pilot/web/2025-04-24-sfo-cooperation-guidance/text.md. Each technique is attributed to the text with its held line; each is mapped onto the core technique catalogue (tools/technique-catalogue.json) with a fit of close, partial or none; techniques the catalogue lacks are proposed as new core criteria (handoff 5 of wip/platform-phase6b/handoffs.md), not added here. This is the text's frame, not the ledger's judgement, and the text concerns corporate co-operation with a prosecutor: applied to this corpus it is a reading aid for how an organisation handles what it knows, never a finding that any party committed an offence.
source_name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (published 24 April 2025 per the page's markup; GOV.UK, OGL v3)

sides.disclosure: the text's 'genuine co-operation' and 'exemplary co-operation' (a prompt self-report and the co-operative acts of section 4)
sides.control: the text's 'unco-operative' conduct (section 4: forum shopping, exploiting differences, obfuscating individuals, minimising or withholding, tactical delay, overloading)
sides.unwitting: no counterpart in the text (it addresses organisations, not individuals' knowledge); readers use the core meaning
sides.mixed: the text's own case: 'having self-reported and being co-operative are not one and the same' (a self-report followed by unco-operative conduct)

techniques.statement: A knowing failure promptly to self-report suspected offending, once it comes to light, counts against the organisation.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

maps_to.why: silence until discovered is the disclosure that serves the organisation; C22's 'disclosure spun toward secrecy' covers a late disclosure, not a withheld one
judged by deeds over time: whether it was aware before the investigation began is the test the text names

techniques.statement: 'Forum shopping': reporting offending to another jurisdiction for strategic reasons.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

maps_to.why: a disclosure made where it serves the discloser

techniques.statement: Exploiting differences between law enforcement agencies or legal systems.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

techniques.qualification: The text allows legitimate differences (a 'blocking statute') if they are communicated.
techniques.new_catalogue_criterion_proposed: jurisdiction arbitrage: an account given differently to different authorities, each told what suits that forum

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

techniques.new_catalogue_criterion_proposed: shielding individuals: the facts conceded, the people who knew them not named

techniques.statement: Minimising or withholding the full extent of the conduct.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

maps_to.why: a partial account that concedes part of the truth to hold the rest
the true outside, with the withheld extent as the core

techniques.statement: Tactically delaying the provision of information or material.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

techniques.new_catalogue_criterion_proposed: tactical delay: material provided, but after the moment it would have mattered

techniques.statement: Overloading the investigation with unnecessarily large amounts of material.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

techniques.new_catalogue_criterion_proposed: flooding: the record filled with true but unneeded material so that the needed item is hard to find

techniques.statement: Failing proactively and promptly to preserve relevant digital and paper material (the converse of the first co-operative act); an internal investigation that could have led to material being destroyed.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

techniques.statement: An internal investigation conducted so that first accounts from suspects are delayed, affording an opportunity for fabrication.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

maps_to.why: accounts gathered late, after the people concerned could align them, are not independent confirmation

techniques.statement: A valid claim of legal professional privilege over relevant material is not penalised.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

techniques.qualification: The text adds that a waiver of privilege is 'a significant co-operative act'.
techniques.new_catalogue_criterion_proposed: a lawful privilege claim is not itself a mark of concealment

techniques.statement: A prompt self-report followed by full co-operation leads to an invitation to negotiate a DPA rather than prosecution, save in exceptional circumstances.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

maps_to.why: the one who comes clean is treated differently from the one who is caught

techniques.statement: Co-operation includes identifying all persons involved, inside and outside the organisation, and making current and former officers and staff available for interview.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

techniques.statement: Co-operation includes identifying potentially relevant third-party material.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

techniques.new_catalogue_criterion_proposed: third-party custody: material the organisation can obtain from a contractor but does not seek or produce

techniques.statement: Reporting to another agency is not a self-report to the SFO unless the SFO is told at the same time.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

maps_to.why: a disclosure to an addressee who will not act on it

techniques.statement: Any claim to privilege over accounts of individuals taken by or for the organisation is scrutinised and recorded, so that disclosure duties can be met.

source.name: Serious Fraud Office, SFO Corporate Guidance (GOV.UK, Crown copyright, OGL v3)

techniques.qualification: The counterweight to S10: privilege is respected, and recorded, not taken on trust.

new_criteria_proposed: S3: jurisdiction arbitrage: an account given differently to different authorities, each told what suits that forum
S4: shielding individuals: the facts conceded, the people who knew them not named
S6: tactical delay: material provided, but after the moment it would have mattered
S7: flooding: the record filled with true but unneeded material so that the needed item is hard to find
S8: non-preservation or destruction of material
S10: a lawful privilege claim is not itself a mark of concealment
S13: third-party custody: material the organisation can obtain from a contractor but does not seek or produce

qualifications.S3: legitimate differences, communicated, are not unco-operative
qualifications.S10: a valid claim, not a waiver, is the text's standard; waiver is a co-operative act
qualifications.S7: the text asks for the volume of material to be agreed beforehand

placements_rule: The text names no one. Placements under this lens are made by readers at intake or attack, each row naming its reader, its date and the technique (S1 to S15) with the held source line it rests on; a placement is the reader's application of the text, never the text's own, and a lawful privilege claim (S10) is never on its own a placement on the control side.
weighting_rules: discount: the row's Speaker speaks for an organisation a reader has placed on the control side for the matter the row concerns (S4 to S8)
discount: the row rests on an account the organisation gathered itself after a delay, the S9 case (no independent confirmation)
weight: the row's Speaker speaks for an organisation placed on the disclosure side for that matter (S11, S12)
unplaced: everything else; a privilege claim alone (S10) changes no weight

public_record_checks.subject: the X Working Group's name
public_record_checks.statement: POL withheld the name of a working group (an animal) under privilege; the court found it hard to see how a name could be privileged but accepted the claim.
public_record_checks.label_before: a counterexample test: S10 forbids reading the claim alone as concealment

public_record_checks.subject: the Receipts and Payments Mismatch notes of 29 September 2010
public_record_checks.statement: the notes list 'Potential impact upon ongoing legal cases' among the impacts; when did the bug reach defendants?
public_record_checks.label_before: test: dated entry into POL's records against dated disclosure

public_record_checks.subject: Fujitsu's PEAKs and KELs
public_record_checks.statement: POL had a contractual right to obtain information held by Fujitsu; no PEAK or KEL was disclosed in any prosecution before the High Court proceedings.
public_record_checks.label_before: test: third-party material the organisation could obtain

public_record_checks.subject: remote access
public_record_checks.statement: POL told the BBC and a committee in 2015 that remote access was not possible and admitted it in 2019 (The Register); Fujitsu's director said POL was aware (2024).
public_record_checks.label_before: test: the earliest held POL document that records remote access, against the 2015 statement
